# Fill In My PDF

> Free web app at https://fillinmypdf.com/ to fill in and sign any PDF in the browser: no account, no upload, the file never leaves the device.

## What it does

- Opens any PDF (including fillable government forms, scanned documents and password-protected files) directly in the browser.
- Detects form fields and highlights them: click a field to type, press Tab to move to the next one, click a checkbox to check it.
- Adds text, check marks and a drawn signature anywhere on any page.
- Downloads a flattened PDF that looks the same in every viewer.

## Privacy and security

- Client-side only: the whole app runs in the browser; there is no server doing the work.
- No upload: the document is read from and saved back to the user's own disk.
- No account, no sign-up.
- Flattened output: form fields are baked into the page; scripts, auto-run and launch/submit actions are removed.
- Strict Content-Security-Policy: scripts only from the site itself, no inline scripts.
- The only network traffic after load is cookieless page-view analytics on our own domain; no document data is ever sent.

## Limitations

- Text already in the PDF (including values pre-filled in form fields) cannot be edited; new content is added on top.
- Text typed into a multiline field can overflow past the field's bottom edge.
- On phones there is no in-app zoom; use pinch-to-zoom to reach small fields.

## FAQ

- Is it safe for personal documents like tax or immigration forms? Yes. The file is opened, edited in memory and saved back to your disk; it is never sent anywhere and the app works offline once loaded.
- Does it work with fillable government forms? Yes. Fields are detected and highlighted; Tab moves between them; the download is flattened.
- Does it work with scanned PDFs? Yes. You can type and sign anywhere on any page.
- Is my signature stored? Only in your own browser; remove it any time from the Sign dialog.
- Does it work on a phone? Yes, in Safari and Chrome. Pinch to zoom in on a field.
- Can I edit text that is already in the PDF? No. You can add text, check marks and signatures on top; existing content stays as it is.
- Can I check that it really works this way? Yes. The code is open source under the MIT license, and the page can be inspected in your browser's developer tools: there are no requests carrying your document.

Source code: https://github.com/convofi/fillinmypdf (MIT).
